name: Earth Crisis
label: Victory
lede: Karl Buechner, a Syracuse skater, spent three years finding four other vegans who didn't drink, then helped invent metalcore with them and took vegan straight edge onto 48 Hours, CNN and, eventually, Geraldo.

eras.title: Looking for vegans in Syracuse
eras.text: Syracuse in a recession, friends struggling with drugs, and a skater who swore off all of it. Buechner's first Earth Crisis died after a few shows; the second was built from another vegan straight edge band, Framework.

years.h: Two Syracuse skaters start Earth Crisis, and it lasts a few shows
years.p: Karl Buechner pitches a band to fellow skater DJ Rose, with Buechner on bass and Rose singing. Jesse Buckley plays drums, John Moseman guitar, and the first Earth Crisis folds after a few gigs.
years.xp:
Rose moved to Syracuse in the summer of 1989. Decibel's book excerpt puts the band's first show in Utica, New York.

Rose went on to book shows instead, and he comes back into the story when Victory Records arrives.

years.cap: Karl Buechner live at Lost Horizon, Syracuse
q: took me from age 18 to age 21 to get a lineup together
years.src: V13: Karl Buechner on Firestorm at 30 · Wikipedia: Karl Buechner · Wikipedia: Earth Crisis
years.h: Karl Buechner swaps bass for the mic and borrows Framework
years.p: Scott Crouse and Ben Read come over on guitars, Ian "Bulldog" Edwards on bass, Michael Riccardi on drums. Buechner now sings.
years.xp:
Buechner met the Framework members at a skateboard demonstration, and Wikipedia says they at first treated Earth Crisis as a Framework side project.

He had gone straight edge at about 15, watching friends struggle with drugs during Syracuse's recession, and vegan by around 18. Finding a line-up where everyone was both took him until he was 21.

years.src: Wikipedia: Earth Crisis · Wikipedia: Breed the Killers
years.h: All Out War fits the whole agenda on one 7-inch
years.p: Earth Crisis's first release, four songs on Conviction Records, lays out straight edge and animal liberation a year before Victory comes calling.
years.xp: One of those songs, Ecocide, got a second life: Earth Crisis re-recorded it as the closing track of Breed the Killers in 1998.

eras.title: The demo that went out the car window
eras.text: Victory's Tony Brummel tossed their tape, then saw them live and changed his mind. Firestorm got hardcore arguing, Destroy the Machines bolted it to metal, and the band ended up explaining veganism on network TV.

years.h: Dennis Merrick and Kris Wiechmann fill two empty seats
years.p: Merrick takes over the drums from Michael Riccardi and Wiechmann takes Ben Read's guitar. With Buechner, Crouse and Ian Edwards, that line-up holds until 1998.

years.big: "threw it out the car window without even listening"
years.h: Dayton changes Tony Brummel's mind about Earth Crisis
years.p: DJ Rose on Victory Records founder Tony Brummel and the band's demo. After seeing Earth Crisis at Ohio's More Than Music festival in 1993, Brummel wanted to put out their record.
years.xp:
Trial's Greg Bennick remembers the question the set raised at More Than Music, in Dayton: was Earth Crisis saying it would round up drug dealers?

Buechner, two years into a history education degree, quit college once Victory signed the band.

years.cap: Earth Crisis at the Bristol Bike Exchange skate park, Bristol, Connecticut
years.p: Four songs and about 15 minutes on Victory Records: Firestorm, Forged in the Flames, Eden's Demise and Unseen Holocaust. Trial's Greg Bennick recalls Maximum Rocknroll and others getting upset.
years.xp:
Wikipedia has the band recording it that summer in Bill Korecky's Cleveland studio, at the start of the All Out War tour. Buechner describes Forged in the Flames as straight edge for life, Eden's Demise as animals and the environment, and Unseen Holocaust as the destruction of indigenous land in the Amazon.

The title song, he says, drew on Black Panther-era writing about communities organizing against drugs. Critics read it as a call to violence, and Demian Johnston of Undertow was among those who objected to the anti-abortion stance in some Earth Crisis songs.

DJ Rose has stressed that Earth Crisis were vegan straight edge, not part of the stricter hardline movement they were often lumped in with.

years.h: Destroy the Machines is built to sound like a hammer hitting something
years.p: Recorded in October and November 1994 at Believer's studio in Pennsylvania, Earth Crisis's first album welds New York hardcore to thrash grooves. NME later named it one of the 15 best hardcore albums ever.
years.xp:
Believer's studio came through a friend, Jim Winters, and the band wanted songs that sounded like "somebody continuously hitting something with a hammer." Buechner, who volunteered at Syracuse's wildlife rehabilitation center, was caring for twelve rescued animals during the 1995 tour.

Kerrang! and Loudwire both put it among the best metalcore albums of all time, Loudwire at number 7. [[Between the Buried and Me|1870fb43-50f1-4660-a879-bb596d1519b6]] covered Forced March in 2006, and the Dutch band Born from Pain and Argentina's Nueva Etica took their names from tracks on it.

years.h: While Merrick heals, Path of Resistance gets started
years.p: With drummer Dennis Merrick injured, Karl Buechner and the rest of Earth Crisis start the side band Path of Resistance, which runs until 2006.
years.xp: Wikipedia puts the injuries down to a touring van accident in 1995, with Merrick hurt worst. The new band drew on Earth Crisis's own past: Michael Riccardi, the drummer Merrick had replaced, and DJ Rose, the first singer, joined another friend in it.

years.src: Decibel · Blabbermouth: Former Earth Crisis frontman
years.h: Earth Crisis explains veganism on MTV, 48 Hours and CNN
years.p: DJ Rose recalls the band on MTV's Smashed, CBS's 48 Hours and CNN's Network Earth, taking vegan straight edge to mainstream viewers.
Earth Crisis's second Victory album pushes metalcore toward something more complex, and the band is asked onto the first Ozzfest.
years.xp: Wikipedia describes Gomorrah's Season Ends as a "more complex and developed form of metalcore," and says the Ozzfest exposure led to a deal with Roadrunner Records.

eras.title: One big-label album, then a hometown goodbye
eras.text: Roadrunner got one record, with Machine Head's Robb Flynn guesting; Victory got the rest. The band called it off on good terms at Hellfest, in Syracuse.

years.cap: Earth Crisis at The Point, Atlanta, 1998
years.h: Ian Edwards gets his brother in the band
years.p: Erick Edwards replaces guitarist Kris Wiechmann, who had played on Earth Crisis's records since 1993. Erick and Ian go on to form Freya with Karl Buechner after the split.

years.cap: Earth Crisis at The Point, Atlanta, 1998
years.h: Roadrunner gets exactly one Earth Crisis album, Breed the Killers
years.p: Andy Sneap produces at Pyramid Studios in Ithaca, New York, and Robb Flynn of [[Machine Head|22a1f4d7-81ff-4216-ac06-3387da6bc118]] sings on One Against All. The band's major-label debut is also its only Roadrunner release.
years.xp:
The album runs 41 minutes 38 seconds. The closer, Ecocide, is a re-recording from All Out War, and Sneap, credited as Screaming Lord Sneap, adds guitar to Ultramilitance.

I Scream Records reissued it in November 2008 with two live bonus tracks.

years.p: After one Roadrunner album, Earth Crisis returns to Victory Records for its fourth studio album.
years.xp: Wikipedia describes Slither as leaning on production and nu metal influence, and says the critical response was mixed.

years.h: Last of the Sane covers Slayer, Led Zeppelin and the Dead Kennedys
years.p: The last album before the 2001 split also includes covers of songs by the Rolling Stones and Cream.

years.cap: Earth Crisis at The Point, Atlanta
years.h: Earth Crisis ends where it started, onstage at Hellfest in Syracuse
years.p: The band splits on good terms, citing members' personal commitments. Karl Buechner starts the metal band Freya the same year.
years.xp: Ian and Erick Edwards joined Buechner in Freya. Scott Crouse and Dennis Merrick moved to California and started Isolated.

eras.title: Straight edge on cable news, then the band comes back
eras.text: Buechner went on Fox News to say straight edge wasn't a gang. Two years later Earth Crisis was back, with the same five men and three more albums.

years.big: a "footnote to the overall Straight Edge story"
q: it's a tragic end on both sides
years.h: Straight edge gets called a gang, and Buechner goes on Geraldo
years.p: Utah and Nevada authorities label straight edge a gang after bat attacks in Reno and a Salt Lake City murder. Karl Buechner, now a former Earth Crisis frontman, goes on Fox News' At Large with Geraldo Rivera to argue the violence is rare.
years.xp:
Buechner told the show straight edge had existed for 25 years with "tens of thousands of believers who are law-abiding, productive people." He said beating someone up over disrespect was "throwing your entire life away."

The police officer on the panel agreed that 90 percent of straight edgers were peaceful and law abiding.

years.h: Earth Crisis reunites at the Maryland Metal and Hardcore Festival
years.p: The Breed the Killers-era five come back and keep going: To the Death (2009) and Neutralize the Threat (2011) on Century Media, then Salvation of Innocents (2014) on Candlelight.
years.xp: The reunion show was January 27, 2007. It was meant as a one-off, but numerous American and European dates followed, and by early 2008 Earth Crisis was headlining Firestorm Fest.

years.src: V13: Karl Buechner on Firestorm at 30
years.h: Firestorm turns 30, and Buechner is still on the road
years.p: Buechner marks the anniversary still fronting Earth Crisis, Freya and Apocalypse Tribe, with shows booked for This Is Hardcore. [[Hatebreed|40b7efb7-1268-4a80-b354-600afdcbe9e2]]'s [[Jamey Jasta|2ae17f26-c50c-4b3b-ac2d-ed5293c03e6c]] is among the singers who cite him as an influence.
years.xp: Recent Earth Crisis shows, Buechner told V13, had included Long Island, Philadelphia, Boston, Buffalo, Syracuse and Alabama. Syracuse "was pretty fun" and "wild," with injuries during the shows.

years.h: Three hours with Buechner on HardLore
years.p: The HardLore podcast sits down with Karl Buechner for nearly three hours on Earth Crisis's history, including where the wrench logo came from. He's now also writing science fiction and fantasy.
